assertion_analysis.tests/test_lifted_holds_read_only_what_w: Fails if the first call does not pass every one of the 5,000 complete report lines to json.loads.
Fails if the independent whole-file reference does not establish a nonempty set smaller than the line count, checking that the fixture contains both lifts and dry-run reports.
Fails if the first incremental result differs from the separately parsed whole-file reference.
Fails if an unchanged second call decodes any line; the recorded base-read mutation reproduces this as assert 5000 == 0.
Fails if the cached second result changes from the independent whole-file result, including a regression that returns an empty set without decoding.
Fails if the next call decodes other than the three newly appended report lines.
Fails if the post-append result differs from a separate whole-file parse of the enlarged log.
Fails if the three new reports do not enlarge the prior lifted set.
Fails if shortening the log does not restart at byte zero and decode all four remaining lines.
Fails if the result after shortening differs from the separate whole-file parse of that shortened log.
Fails if the larger log's prior answer survives after the file is shortened.
Fails if the initial six-line history is not observed before testing replacement.
Fails if the longer replacement at a new inode is treated as an append instead of decoding all twelve replacement lines.
Fails if the replacement result differs from the separate whole-file parse of the replacement file.
Fails if the old file's lifted pair is retained after replacement.
Fails if the decoder sees the unterminated half-line or misses any of the twenty complete lines; clamp-mutation.log records the removed-clamp regression as assert 21 == 20.
Fails if the partial-read result differs from a separate whole-file parse, which ignores the malformed trailing fragment.
Fails if the incomplete report is counted as a lifted hold before its newline arrives.
Fails if the stored append offset advances past the last newline while the half-line remains on disk.
Fails if completing the fragment produces zero or more than one decoder call.
Fails if the completed report's expected pair is not added to the lifted set.
Fails if the completed-read result differs from the separate whole-file parse.
Fails if the seed call does not return all twenty expected lifted pairs.
Fails if the seed call does not decode its twenty complete lines.
Synchronization assertion: fails if the test does not release the held first reader within five seconds.
Fails if the first reader does not reach the append reader within five seconds, so the planned overlap cannot proceed.
Fails if either concurrent reader raises an exception.
Fails if either concurrent reader remains alive after its five-second join.
Fails if overlapping reads lose any of the twenty seeded or three appended pairs; race-negative-control.log shows the split-lock mutation fails here with only the appended pairs retained.
Fails if any line is handed to the decoder more than once during the concurrent reads and final check.
Fails if the decoder sees any payload other than the three appended lines or misses one of them.

assertion_independence: No assertion compares the function result with the same object passed to it: result sets use a separate whole-file parser or a separately enumerated fixture set, while decode counts and payloads come from the recording json.loads wrapper. The expected race pairs are generated from fixture indices rather than the returned set.
